Subject: MSA + Order Form: IP scope checklist and next steps

Karthik / Marcus —

We received DataWave's redlines (attached PDF). High level: they want (1) explicit customer ownership of all outputs; (2) a strict "no training" carve-out unless they opt in; (3) a broader feedback license carve-in that they want restricted. Sales wants to keep things simple: customer owns outputs for their internal use, but we need rights to use anonymized feedback to improve models and metrics (no PII training, carve out regulated data).

I put together a short checklist and a proposed alternative clause in the attached RI_proposed_ip_clauses.docx. Key asks for Legal:
- Approve the proposed feedback license language (non-exclusive, limited to internal model improvement, aggregate/anonymized only, with exclusions for customer-designated sensitive data).
- Confirm acceptable phrasing for an explicit "no training" default with an opt-in orderform checkbox that both parties sign.
- Flag any redlines in the MSA that would create transfer or sublicensing exposure (we should not grant broad rights to use outputs to build competing services).

Timing: DataWave is pushing to close next week to align with their procurement window. Sales (Karthik) will push for a single redline pass and an orderform checkbox for training.

Can you please review the clause in the docx and respond with either: approved / needs edits / need to escalate to outside counsel, by EOD tomorrow? If needs edits, please include language I can send to DataWave.

Thanks —
Evelyn

Thanks Evelyn — quick commercial context: DataWave is a strategic PLG customer; they run search and recommendation use cases and expect predictable unit economics. Their legal is conservative on training because they fear model leakage, but product wants the ability to opt-in for a fine-tuned private variant later.

From Sales POV the ideal outcome:
- Customer owns output for their application (we're OK with that).
- We keep a narrow feedback license limited to "improvements to the Redwood service" and explicitly exclude using customer data to create a stand-alone competing model or to sell a model to third parties.
- We surface a clear opt-in on the Order Form for "Use of Customer Data for Model Training/Improvement" with toggles for (i) aggregate/implied metrics only, (ii) fine-tune/private variant (explicit paid opt-in).

If Legal can sign off on the language in RI_proposed_ip_clauses.docx (I reviewed and it looks balanced), I'll send the follow-up to Amanda at DataWave today and propose a DocuSign flow for the orderform checkbox.

—Karthik

Evelyn / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from Legal/Product:
1) Output ownership: we are asking for explicit assignment of "output" (as defined in our redline). We need to be able to use output to operate our product and integrate into our downstream services; we do not intend to grant you rights to redistribute our outputs outside our organization.
2) Training: we will not agree to any language that allows Redwood to train on content that includes customer PII or regulated categories (PHI, financial account numbers) at any time. For non-sensitive content, we are open to a time-bound, reversible opt-in that we can toggle off.
3) Feedback license: we cannot sign a broad perpetual license for feedback. We can agree to a limited-term, royalty-free license to use feedback for product/back-end improvements provided you: (a) do not include verbatim customer content in training datasets, (b) maintain an audit trail of what was used, and (c) provide an export of redactions on request.

I can take your proposed language and provide redline edits, but we need a response to the three bullets above by EOD Monday so legal can finish procurement approval.

Thanks,
Amanda Park
Head of Procurement | DataWave Solutions

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: IP scope checklist and next steps

Evelyn / Karthik —

I reviewed RI_proposed_ip_clauses.docx and the DataWave redlines. Summary of recommended position and edits:

1) Output ownership: Accept assignment of output to customer for their internal business use. Add an express carve-out: Redwood retains rights to (a) use non-identifiable statistical outputs for benchmarking, (b) generate aggregate usage metrics, and (c) use derived, non-attributable insights to improve the service. Proposed sentence: "Customer retains ownership of Output; provided, however, that Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified Output and derived metrics for model improvement and service analytics, provided such use does not permit reconstruction of Customer-provided content."

2) Training/No-Train default: Approve a "no training" default in the MSA with an opt-in in the Order Form. The opt-in language must be narrow and include: scope (only models specified), duration (e.g., 12 months), and exclusions (PII/regulatory categories). We should require Customer to represent that any data designated for training is not subject to third-party confidentiality obligations.

3) Feedback license: Resist a perpetual, unlimited feedback license. Offer a 24-month, non-exclusive, royalty-free license limited to improving Redwood's hosted inference and operational tooling. Explicit prohibition on using customer content to train third-party models or commercialize a customer-specific model outside of a paid private-delivery contract. Include auditability language (we will track what was used).

I am attaching a draft redline (OrderForm-v3.pdf) with inline edits. If you want me to take the edits to DataWave Legal, I can, but given the commercial timeline you may prefer Sales to present the compromise.

Action items:
- Karthik: if Sales is comfortable, share our proposed language with Amanda and propose the orderform checkbox DocuSign flow (target: today).
- Evelyn: escalate to me if DataWave insists on perpetual training rights — we will need a narrower commercial concession (e.g., higher fee/extended term) to compensate.

Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: OrderForm-v3.pdf (annotated)

Amanda —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is the redline Marcus prepared (OrderForm-v3.pdf) and a one-paragraph summary you can share internally. High-level compromise:
- Output: Customer owns Output; Redwood may use de-identified aggregate outputs and derived metrics for service improvement; no right to resell customer-specific models.
- Training: Default = no training. Order Form checkbox allows (i) aggregate/metrics usage, and separately (ii) opt-in to paid fine-tune/private variant. Exclusions: PII, PHI, financial account numbers unless specifically listed and consented.
- Feedback license: 24-month, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use feedback for product/back-end improvements only; audit trail and right to request export of redactions.

Karthik will propose the DocuSign flow with the orderform checkbox this afternoon. If this looks acceptable in principle, can we confirm the timeline (EOD Monday) for legal sign-off? Evelyn
